name: ab_perfect_def
statement: (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) : Nat.Perfect n ↔ ∑ d ∈ Nat.divisors n, d = 2 * n
closed: ∀ (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n), Nat.Perfect n ↔ ∑ d ∈ Nat.divisors n, d = 2 * n
informal: Paper's definition of perfect (divisors sum to exactly 2n) agrees with Mathlib's Nat.Perfect for positive n.
original: An abundant number is an integer n whose divisors add up to more than 2n. A perfect number is an integer n whose divisors add up to exactly 2n.
type: ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < n → (n.Perfect ↔ ∑ d ∈ n.divisors, d = 2 * n)
